verdict: No free, unauthenticated source provides a complete observed-liquidation census with defensible provenance and adequate coverage. Track A (observed liquidation labels) is NOT viable and is formally closed. Pivot to Track B (modeled boundary-breach) with a new experiment ID, using the best available free mark-price + margin-parameter data, clearly labeled as a modeled proxy per RESEARCH_PROMPT.md section 15.
rationale: Six candidate source families enumerated, probed, and recorded in fclr_tracks01_source_registry_20261123T014600Z.{json,md}: Binance public archive, Bybit public REST, OKX public REST, Hyperliquid public API, Ironflow/Hugging Face archive, public GitHub/Zenodo/HF/institutional archives.
Binance public archive returns HTTP 200 for metrics/funding/klines zips but liquidationSnapshot returns HTTP 404 on both daily and monthly paths — no observed-liquidation dataset.
Bybit public REST returns HTTP 403 on all probed endpoints — not an unauthenticated source in this environment (RESEARCH_PROMPT.md section 1: no credentials, no bypass).
OKX public REST returns HTTP 200 for candles/funding but HTTP 404 for its liquidation endpoint — no observed-liquidation dataset.
Hyperliquid public API returns HTTP 405 (GET /info; POST required) and no verified unauthenticated historical liquidation endpoint with deep history.

Ironflow/Hugging Face serves real observed liquidation events (HTTP 200 PAR1 parquet, CC BY 4.0, unauthenticated) but is a capped-sample feed, not a complete census (RESEARCH_PROMPT.md section 15; AGENT_HANDOFF.md on-disk inputs). Absence cannot be labeled zero.
No GitHub/Zenodo/HF institutional liquidation URL verified admissible.

track_a_closure_evidence.structural_impossibility_basis: access terms (Bybit 403), absent endpoints (Binance liquidationSnapshot 404, OKX liquidation 404), method gating (Hyperliquid 405 / POST-only), and incomplete coverage (Ironflow capped sample). Three distinct blocked routes spanning two+ source families (RESEARCH_PROMPT.md section 16).
